payload.adrs:
ADR-1 VENDOR-QR-ENCODER: vendor a small proven QR library (source into tools/vendor, no npm) for the Encode function. Addresses R3 (scannability - correctness is field-proven) + R4 (install - vendoring is permitted). Rejected: hand-roll (K1, correctness risk - kept as the fallback), npm-install (dependency risk).
ADR-2 CONFIG-WRITE-AMENDMENT: the engine writing phone.json (a secret) is permitted, amending se.adr-phone-secret-machine-local; the write is ATOMIC (temp + rename). Addresses R5 + R1. Owner-confirmed. Rejected: direct write (non-atomic, partial-config risk).
ADR-3 LOCAL-ONLY-ENCODE: the topic is encoded on our side; no external image/QR service is contacted. Addresses R2 (secrecy) + se.adr-answer-authenticity. Rejected: a hosted QR API (leaks the topic).
